html:
An interlude written in an unusual manner for the cycle: a talkative omniscient storyteller turns to a "shrewd reader" and for the time being hides the main secrets. The main character is a gray-haired prophet, the former king of Shimmery Francis-Ilian, and next to him all the time is an unkempt beggar, whose identity is revealed only in the finale. The name refers to the custom of Darkwater: a stranger gets to the queen only if he is believed by three of her trusted vassals.

Plot

The beggar at the gate

At the entrance to Nan Clair, the capital of the swamp kingdom, two guys beat up a dirty lanky beggar. The guards did not let him into the city dirty, and he in revenge threw swamp hedges at everyone who wanted to enter: “All will be grrr-ryazny!” The white-bearded prophet in gray, whom the guard meets with honor, asks the fighters. The beggar immediately throws a lump of dirt into the elegant companion of the prophet, Gerion. The prophet stops Gerion grasping at the dagger and tells him to let the beggar into the city with his entourage. The beggar, in response, calls the "wise" fool, who escaped into the swamp "from the sun, wine and women."

Who is the Prophet

The narrator, referring to the "astute reader", reveals the background. Nine years ago, on the eve of the Days of Abundance, the prophet spent the night at the Maximian monastery on the edge of the Boneless Failure and saw a dream. (Bottomless Abyss) Shocked, he stayed there for eight years to study the works of the Foremothers and Forefathers and about once a year saw new prophetic dreams. His fame spread throughout the South. He was formerly the Francis-Ilian of Sophia the Great, King of Shimmery. Lord Telurian stood up at his appearance. One day he bought the island for a single walk with his beloved, he had one son, sixteen daughters and countless altessa. After his sleep, he abdicated the throne in favor of his son.

Three months before the events of the interlude, the prophet with a retinue of seven people left the monastery, bypassing the war at Melorange and Faunterra. In the town of Surlion in the Holliwell Delta, he predicted to the Litlanders that Adrian would defeat the Steppes. (Hollywell) He told the merchants about a dream where the ships went “without joy and wind,” and asked the ship given to him to give to the Maximian brothers, having made only one voyage on it. In Leonhard, the sea gate of Hope, the prophet learned that his prophecy had come true. He interpreted the dream of Yangmei and Agatha sharing a bed as reconciliation of the North with the Crown. In the underground sanctuary of the temple of Elena-Na-Wave, he took in his hands a small flickering object, which for three centuries no one dared to touch, and remained unharmed. The object was given to him, and he ordered to lock him in a bronze box inside a cast iron chest. He told Count Lighthart that the worst days of his house were behind him. In the Heart of the World, the Duke of Farway grieved for his grandsons-hostages. (Heart of Light; Henry Farway) The prophet told him about the dream of a girl saved from the clutches of the monster, and the next day came the news of the death of the Lord Adrian: the war was over, and Farway’s grandchildren survived. As a gift, the prophet received the “Divine Mechanics” of the Forefather Edward.

He did not reveal his vision to anyone. In the first dream, the world was bent by a funnel, and all living things slipped into the Boneless Failure, and then the Universal Spiral itself split. For eight years, the prophet did not find in the writings of the Forebears any interpretation: the Forebears believed that the world was eternal, and the dream would sound the worst heresy. The last hope he considered Lady in Darkness, "the wisest woman of the South." (Lady in the Dark) She survived three children and three husbands, knew four emperors, and mastered both Vedic arts.

Gerion

In the city, the beggar takes two bags of food and drink from the prophet and leaves, without even asking what he dreamed: “Find Baba, tell her dreams.” In the alley, Gerion puts a dagger to his nostril and tells him not to be seen again. The narrator reports that Gerion is one of the seven who came out with the prophet from the monastery, and has served him since the time when he still bore another name. A foreigner cannot enter the palace of the nobility until the “gate of trust” passes, so the retinue settles in a hotel that looks like an anthill. At dinner, Gerion consoles the prophet with colorful parables that the key may be nearby, “with the mouth of an old acquaintance.” The prophet knows that the gods do not speak with the mouth of Gerion. At night, Gerion sends Nan-Claire's grimmest cab driver somewhere for the silver gloria.

Statue of the Forefather Kristen

The next morning, a crowd of half a thousand people silently follows the prophet to the Cathedral of Kristen. On the steps, three beggars beat the fourth, the same acquaintance: he took their place and threatens to become the “general of beggars”. The priest in the green robe, Father Loris, leads the guests to the balcony above the altar. The prophet also takes a beggar with him: he meets a second time in his path, and maybe the gods want to say something. The Prophet briefly answers the questions of the parishioners. To the apprentice in love, he says, “If you love, it’s already a success.” To the grim warrior in the cloak of disguise, who asks whether to take up the case, he answers the parable of an unsharpened axe.

The shrine is a sacred object, a living figure of the Forefather Kristen in a third of human growth with a candle extinguished in his hand. The figure is covered with boils and ulcers, and on the hand with a candle there is no skin. According to legend, Kristen and her brother Edward studied the forces by which the gods rule the world. Over the years, Kristen decided that he had grasped the laws of divine authority, and the gods mutilated his statue. He repented, burned the notes, and Edward wrote Divine Mechanics instead. The statue heals fever, rash, and “shameful illnesses.” The prophet notices that the candle is made rough, without a wick and drops of wax. He asks to cover the statue with a cloak of Gerion, like a tent, and in the dark around the candle three "flowers" of curved rays appear: red, blue and whitish, and the candle itself flickers weakly. The Prophet explains that he derived this from Divine Mechanics: Kristen studied the flickering Objects.

The beggar scrapes himself all the time, mutters “Bad”, “Mischief”, and then runs away with a scream, falls down the stairs and on a slippery floor. In the square, the prophet gives him a golden Hilt, and the beggar in horror recoils. Father Loris admits that he is the first gate: the prophet and Gerion passed them, “the poor man also passed the first gate. Shame he doesn’t know that.”

Cribola and Pits

After midnight, a note tells Gerion to walk two hundred steps. The man in the cloak immobilizes him with a sticky hot glove and leads him to a room hung with herbs. It's a "cribola sting," a swamp poisoner. He does not kill for money, but sells Gerion a weapon with the condition not to kill anyone in Darkwater. The weapon is three corzo seeds, a bush, half a plant, half an animal. A rhythmic sound, two passes and a kick, wakes the seeds, and they jump to a target marked with two brown stripes, from a distance of up to a hundred steps. The seed bites through the canvas, but not the skin, and kills in about a minute without an antidote. Two more Elena Gerion pays for some "strange request". Then the poisoner shows him the Pits - city drains, where rats swarm, rattlesnake that devour sewage and purify the water. Rats are afraid of screaming, but they will eat someone who can neither scream nor move.

Tops of the Dark Kings

On the third day, a beggar at a port fair plays the "veteran" of the Battle of Melorange, where, according to him, a spark kills the soul. He complains to the prophet that Gerion threatened him with a knife, and admits that he hates trains, letters and writing. Admiral Fanno Groc, the Foltician, the Queen's "first navigator", takes guests by boat on the Tops of the Dark Kings, a lagoon beyond the Foltic Islands where the water is black from algae. There are three safe fairways, and all three know only eight pilots. The admiral talks about the Foltic belief in "equal power" and prophecy: in three hundred years, Polaris will split into a hundred thousand islets, because the lords build too many castles, and the knights forge too much armor. According to him, when Polaris cracks and Bottomless Fail fills with water, an empty inflated fur will pop up with a note: “We were here first. The sailors of Volta, the sixth century."

Half a mile into the water, a half-sinked schooner sticks out. Five years ago, she was “captured by the Dark Ones”: she strayed off the fairway, and the stems covered her keel. The beggar says, “Mrrazi. Destroyed the ship, and they are happy!” — and the admiral looks at him with great respect. Groc gives a note: the second gate is passed. The prophet and the beggar agree that he will “pay” for help, finally asking about sleep and expressing his opinion.

The Past of Gerion

The same poisoner under the guise of an amulet dealer sells Gerion a pillow with two scarlet features, and he hangs it with annoyance to the laugh of the prophet and the beggar. The narrator reveals the story of Gerion. Ten years ago, his father, a rich southerner, got him the place of adjutant to the king, and two years passed “in a fairy tale”. Then the king drank with the abbot, saw a dream, recanted and locked himself in the library. Most of the courtiers went to the court of Prince Hector, and Gerion remained: he thought that this was another whim, like the time when the king “abolished the winter”. (Hector of Shimmery) Five years ago, he asked to be released from the oath, but the prophet replied that he would let him go when he heard the words of the gods through him. Since then, Gerion has been selling the secrets of the master. The first dream he interprets as a harbinger of the death of the prophet himself: a man is himself a whole world.

Third Gate

On the sixth day, Lord Emmon Darklin, the royal castle's castellans, a purebred Yankee and the Queen's nephew are called in. The castle stands behind a "rope" of net grass, in fact a quagmire, and the only bridge is guarded by the granite Bridge Tower, where Emmon lives. The beggar is washed away by this time: he resisted, referring to the commandments, “accept his place in the world with dignity” and “Let the other be.” Gerion dressed him in white stockings, blue breeches and black patterned galley and sewed corzo seeds under the lining. In the morning, he put two brown stripes on the gray robe of the prophet. His plan is to “save” the king from an assassination attempt at the right moment, to prove that the first dream foreshadowed the death of the prophet, to return him to the throne and become the first minister.

Emmon stares at the guests for a few minutes, then jokingly asks what they dreamed, and arranges a test. He offers two bowls: harmless rain water and a tincture of lilanna, a deadly poison. The prophet takes a cup of poison with a bow and drinks, the beggar drinks water, Gerion refuses both. Then Emmon explains: the water became poison when it was poured into a mug of tomma wood, and the smoke of candles from the wax of the illary causes a throat spasm, from which only a sip of any liquid saves. The beggar writhes, but survives: in low concentration, the juice of the tomma does not kill. A suffocating Gerion drinks lilanna at the last moment. The prophet does not suffer at all: when shaking hands, Emmon applied a neutralizer to his palm. The lesson is trust in the master. All three pass through the gate:

“The gate is not all-knowing, but sincere.”

In the castle guests are carried a short yellow rail wagon: so the Queen teaches to know to spark technique. The beggar screams in panic that he hates trains, and Gerion notices scars from his teeth on his left forearm.

Moths Hall

The Throne Room is a glass greenhouse with butterflies, birds and a pond with pitchers. A blind, dried-up Lady-in-the-Dark sits in a braided chair under the plaid, next to her lady Gerda. The Queen asks each guest to choose a flower. The prophet takes a thin blade of grass — hope. Gerion chooses the lush rose, "the majesty and luxury of your majesty's court." The beggar brings a black cross-shaped flower, a "symbol of hopelessness". The queen claps her hands three times, and the seeds in the beggar's gall wake up, but while the prophet is sitting on a bench, the seeds do not see the stripes on his back. There are three “gates” out of the labyrinth and they call who they saw. Loris saw a noble man with a broken destiny and a low gold lover. Groc is a "bloody seafaring lord" and a "silly spy-dog." Emmon recognized the venal southerner, from whom he bought information about his master through intermediaries for eight years, and “Lord Manson Louise of the Yangmei family”, a conspirator, court jester and king-killer. The beggar replies, “Will you pour the wine to the king-killer?”

Gerion declares Manson a spy of the North and turns the prophet with his back to the seeds, going to rush across. But Manson spits, "unfolds", and leaves, and the seeds lose their purpose. The Prophet states that Manson is not a murderer. The jester is tormented at the sight of Hilt, that is, Adrian, Sacred Objects, letters and trains reminiscent of the disaster on the Back, and cannot be on the side of the northerner. Manson is crying.

Then the prophet reveals his. Eight years ago, he was invited to visit the Second of the Five, the abbot of the Maximian monastery, the keeper of the Proval and the Queen's brother in the secret order, and offered to join the order. That night, a dream came. The Prophet sent vassals to learn about the order for years. He learned that the order suggested to the imperial scientists the idea of “waves”, makes believable fakes of objects, discovered the amazing properties of flickering and has secret enemies. Gerion, the most limited and greedy of the vassals, he kept with him on purpose: dictated to him letters about insignificant matters, and he traded his secrets. One link from the buyers of Gerion led to Emmon, the other to the son of the prophet. Now he gives Gerion to the Queen to feed his enemies with lies. Upon Gerion's cry for freedom, the prophet replies that the vassal oath is not a contract.

Corzo seeds

At this moment, Manson stands up, the seeds see the stripes on the back of the prophet and stick into it. The prophet feels only itching, then writhes in pain and cannot straighten up. The Queen says that the order knows the danger threatening the world, and that it echoes the Foltian prophecy. Behind, a voice familiar to Gerion is heard: the sting of the crybola, placed by the queen to the prophet, removes the seeds and announces that "someone prudent" has long devastated their poisonous sacs. The back of the prophet, which he pulled, trying to scratch, the poisoner corrects. Unmoved Gerion is carried away, his fate will be decided by the prophet.

Ulyana Dust and Tree

Manson refuses to trust the Queen, his "brother's mother-in-law" who called his father a fool. He rips off her blanket, throws himself and hisses in her face, Admiral, Emmon, Loris and the lady: "Will you kill the emperor? Kill Adrian!" Then he falls in sobs: “None of you?.. Help me find it..." - and shows bite marks. Emmon guesses that the jester forced Ulyanina Dust, a drug passed on in a letter and subduing the will. (Ulyana's Dust) The queens are confused. They say that Dust was hit in Almera on the day of the fall of the bridge, that the northerner is a "serpovka" and does not know whose, that the archer has gone astray and "owns the Secret". According to them, “the Tree is swaying”, “the Serpent” gained strength after the “Seventeenth Gift”, and the world has not three hundred years left, but several. They demand extreme measures. The Queen refuses. The second of the Five acted on his own will, and it will not happen again. The Serpent means nothing to the Tree, and the Seventeenth Gift only brought the Day of Salvation closer.

Departure

Lady-in-the-Dark decides to go to the capital to meet with the "northerner and the one who calls himself the Peace Bearer". The prophet agrees. Manson, too, after he hesitates: he shows pantomime as the imperial executioners cut him into pieces. The Queen promises to testify in his favor, and Francis-Ilian quotes Pramatery Yumin's work "Justice and Action": the crime committed under the influence of Ulyanina Dust is not guilty. Three days later, the motorcades are performing. On the way, Francis-Ilian enters the secret order and learns two secrets: what Tree his brothers are raising and what split Polaris faces in three hundred years if the Tree does not hold the world together with its roots. They are not revealed to the reader.

Characters

  • Francis-Ilian is the former king of Shimmery of the genus Sophia the Great, a dreamer prophet.
  • Manson Louise of the Yangmei family is a former court jester of Adrian, hiding under the guise of a beggar.
  • Lady in the Dark is the blind queen of Darkwater. Fraileen Gerd is with her.
  • Gerion is the adjutant of the prophet, the son of a wealthy southern family, a spy and a conspirator.
  • Father Loris (first gate), Admiral Fanno Grok (second), Lord Emmon Darklin (third) - the "gate of trust".
  • "The sting of kribola" - a swamp poisoner in the service of the Queen, a gloomy warrior in a cloak of disguise.

Significance in the Series

The interlude reveals that Manson is alive and under the influence of Ulyanina Dust raised his hand on Adrian (the joker believes that he killed him; it later turns out that the emperor survived), and brings to the stage two players who will play a huge role in the "Yanmean Hunt": Lady in Darkness and Francis-Ilian. (Ulyana's Dust; The Yanmei Hunt; Lady in the Dark) Here, for the first time, a secret order is manifested, which "grows a Tree" (later it will be called Gardeners), to which the queen and the abbot of the Maximian monastery belong - the Second of the Five. The prophecy of the death of Polaris and the dream of Failure set one of the deepest mysteries of the cycle.

Three "gates" appear again in the main story. In "Janmei Hunt", Lady in Darkness introduces Minerva to her companions, Lord Emmon Darklin and Admiral Fanno Grok, and upon arrival in the capital, Emmon assures Erwin that the queen is suffering from a disease, although he suspects poison. (The Yanmei Hunt) Cribola stings guard the queen and try her food. In Fantasias, Emmon, "the nephew of the late Lady in Darkness", contests Darkwater's throne with Mireille Nan-Claire and asks Prince Hector to shackle her. (Fantasies; Mireille Nen-Clair)

Trivia

  • The story is told on behalf of a talkative narrator who directly addresses the "astute reader", runs ahead ("his unholy plea was heard"), and for the time being conceals the names.
  • In the text there is a discrepancy in the timing. It is said that the prophet visited the monastery "nine years ago" and spent eight years there, but both the first dream and the invitation of the Second of the Five are attributed to "eight years ago."
  • Once Francis-Ilianus “abolished winter” in Shimmery, decreed to consider December, January and February “young spring”.
  • The beggar refers to the commandments of the Foremothers, so as not to wash: the first is “accept your place in the world with dignity” and the twelfth is “Let the other be.”
